speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin assessing your chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis, could you please tell me your age and if you have a history of smoking or occupational exposure to dust and chemicals?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. I need to ask if you have ever had fever, weight loss, or coughing up blood, and whether there is any family history of lung disease or similar symptoms in your relatives.

text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience shortness of breath during exertion, and have you noticed any clubbing of your fingers or toes? Please also confirm if there is any family history of chronic lung disease.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text:
You have denied shortness of breath and systemic symptoms, but the chronic production of copious purulent sputum is highly suggestive of bronchiectasis rather than simple bronchitis. I will request a high-resolution CT scan of the chest to confirm airway dilation and check for clubbing on physical exam.

REQUEST TEST: High-Resolution CT Chest
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text:
The CT scan results are reported as normal, which makes bronchiectasis less likely given the classic symptoms of copious purulent sputum. I need to clarify if you have a history of frequent sinus infections or nasal polyps, and whether you have any known allergies or asthma.

REQUEST TEST: Sweat Chloride Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the sweat chloride test is normal, cystic fibrosis is effectively ruled out. Given your chronic cough with copious purulent sputum but a normal CT scan, I need to ask if you have ever been diagnosed with asthma or if you experience wheezing, as this could suggest non-CF bronchiectasis or severe chronic bronchitis. Do you have a history of allergic rhinitis or sinusitis?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, weight loss, night sweats, or shortness of breath.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the copious purulent sputum and recurrent infections despite a normal CT and sweat chloride test, I suspect Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia or another ciliary defect. Do you have a history of chronic sinusitis, hearing loss, or infertility, and was your birth complicated by respiratory distress?

REQUEST TEST: Nasal Nitric Oxide Measurement

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: RESULTS: Nasal Nitric Oxide: 15 nL/min (Low; Normal is typically >200 nL/min, suggesting Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia)

speaker: Doctor
text:
The low nasal nitric oxide level strongly supports a diagnosis of Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia, explaining your chronic sputum production and recurrent infections despite normal CT and sweat chloride results.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia
